name: Hitbox / Hurtbox
description: Frame-data-accurate collision for fighting games: per-move box sets keyed to animation phases (startup, active, recovery), overlap resolution with priority, and trade detection when both sides connect on the same frame. It exists because combat.melee_basic answers 'a swing happened' while a fighting game needs 'this rectangle was live for exactly frames 9 through 14' — the difference between an action game and a genre where whiff punishing is the core skill. This component owns the boxes and the contact facts, and deliberately nothing downstream of contact: damage numbers, scaling, and knockback belong to combat.damage_resolver, cancel timing to combat.combo_chain, and invulnerability display to presentation. Boxes attach to movement.character_body so they track the body through knockback and throws without a second transform pipeline.

inputs.name: moveDataTable
inputs.description: Per-move records: startup / active / recovery frame spans and the hitbox rectangles live during active frames. Frame data is the game — this table is where a designer's intent becomes measurable.

inputs.name: hitPriority
inputs.description: Tiebreak class when overlapping hitboxes contest the same hurtbox on the same frame. Higher wins; equal priorities trade.

inputs.name: invulnerableFrameSpans
inputs.description: Frame ranges during which this fighter's hurtboxes are withdrawn — invincible reversals, throw techs. Declared per move, not granted ad hoc, so invulnerability is auditable frame data.

inputs.name: teamId
inputs.description: Friendly-fire filter. In versus play each fighter is their own team; the field exists so assist and tag variants do not hit their own side.

outputs.name: currentFramePhase
outputs.description: startup, active, or recovery for the move in flight — the single fact training-mode overlays and AI both read.
